- Primary constraints: p95 latency <= 250ms for real-time previews (25–50 token outputs), throughput target ~100 RPS during peak, strict PII redaction and audit logging.
- Recommended approach: run a small eval suite (your prompt set + ours) across two model families (7B and 13B quantized variants) to measure quality vs cost/latency tradeoffs.

Actions we will take (by EOD Fri unless we hear otherwise):
1) Share Redwood-verified benchmark pack and the sample prompt set we used for similar finance customers (link + PDF attached).
2) Dylan will provide model recommendations & perf numbers (TPS, p50/p95 latency percentiles) and call out any known quality regressions for the prompts you shared.
3) Marissa will follow up on procurement timeline and any required PO/contract steps.
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive next week to review eval results and decide a pilot configuration.

Attaching: redwood-verified-benchmarks-202606.pdf (benchmarks + methodology). Also posting the prompt set link in the next message so you can drop in your examples.

Hi Jamie — following up with the initial model recommendations and the performance profiles we maintain as Redwood-verified references. Notes below are for the prompts you described (~40 tokens output on average). We ran these on our Dedicated A100 pools (configuration: 40G A100 instances, FP16 / quantized kernels where applicable).

Recommended candidates: 
1) redwood-open-7b-v2 (smaller, cost-efficient)
   - Typical throughput: ~240 TPS (tokens/sec)
   - End-to-end response latency (40 tokens): p50 ~60ms, p95 ~180ms
   - Strengths: strong for high-throughput classification/extraction with lower cost; fewer hallucinations on constrained templates after prompt engineering.

2) redwood-large-13b-q4 (balanced latency/quality)
   - Typical throughput: ~110 TPS
   - End-to-end response latency (40 tokens): p50 ~120ms, p95 ~250ms
   - Strengths: higher factuality / better entity extraction out-of-the-box; recommended if your tolerance for manual verification is low.

Quality notes & regressions: 
- On the sample extraction prompts you shared, the 7B variant had a ~4.2% false-entity rate on our finance prompt set; 13B-q4 dropped to ~1.6%. We'll include a per-entity breakdown in the eval.
- Hallucination detection: we recommend coupling the model output with a verification pass (matching against ledger fields or regex-based checks). We can run an automatic precision/recall sweep during the eval.

Benchmarks & links (attached + shared):
- Redwood verified perf pack (methodology + raw metrics): https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/2026-q2/redwood-verified-benchmarks.pdf
- Eval prompt set (example + Finex template merger): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cRedwood/finex-evals (I copied your sample and merged in our QA prompts).

Attachments included in this message: redwood-verified-benchmarks-202606.pdf (benchmarks + test harness results).

Next steps I propose:
- Run the merged prompt set (we'll drop in the Finex sample) against redwood-open-7b-v2 and redwood-large-13b-q4; deliver a short report with per-entity precision/recall, hallucination rate, and the latency percentiles you requested. ETA: 72 hours after you confirm the prompt set is final.
- Schedule a 60-min tech deep-dive (Dylan + Finex ML infra + Alex) to walk results and pilot config.

If that works, Alex / Marissa — can you confirm dates for the deep-dive next week? Jamie — when your team is ready, drop any additional prompt variants into the Drive folder and we'll pick them up.

Thanks,
